label: late original-phase "e" in sequences starting with x/h
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.03% of steps). It fires almost only in the original phase at positions 4-8, peaking at 5-6, with about 2% of its mass at the delimiter and none in the copy phase. The strongest driver is the input token "e" (14x lift, 55% of mass), and it is strongly gated by the first token of the sequence being x (20x lift, 72% of mass) or h (4x). Every top activation is "e" at step 5-6 in a sequence starting with x or h, often right after y. The predicate "e at t>=4 with first token x/h" catches 48% of the top-quartile activations but only 17% of the bottom quartile; the weak activations are scattered over other tokens in late original positions of x/h-initial sequences. Precision is low (most such "e" steps stay inactive), so some unidentified context also matters. It never fires at t<4 or in the copy phase.
